title: The ribbon that comes back inside out

data.source: Pancharatnam (1956); Berry (1984); Aharonov and Anandan (1987); Samuel and Bhandari (1988). Computed for spin-half states on loops of the Bloch sphere.

prediction: On a great-circle loop of spin-half states the geometric phase, measured from the start of the occasion, is 0 up to the half-turn and pi after it, so the spinor's sign flip sits exactly at the cut; on a tilted loop there is no jump and the cut carries only half of a smaller phase.
baseline: Pancharatnam's phase (1956) and Berry's geometric phase (1984): a spin-half state carried round a loop returns multiplied by exp(-i Omega / 2).
why: On the great circle the phase stayed at 0, jumped to pi exactly half-way round, and stayed there: the sign flip of a spinor arrives all at once at the cut, because the cut is where the state is orthogonal to the occasion's start. That is Pancharatnam's theorem and adds nothing to it. On a tilted loop nothing jumped. The count (two cuts per loop) is the same for every loop while the phase is not; coherence fixes the phase only for circles and otherwise only bounds it.
